`Claim:` session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S` · branch `claude/issue-8497-detail-section-group-and-labels`

Claimed by the `domain:ui` PM seat on behalf of the dev it is dispatching. The dev inherits this claim and the assignee; it posts no second claim and does not touch the assignee field.

The card body is the brief — it carries two defects, and they are not the same shape:

1. **An authored `sections[].group` THROWS and takes every sibling section down**, while both the spec's docs and this renderer's own docs predict a silent no-op.
2. **An enumerated `sections[].fields` resolves labels only through the i18n bundle** — with none, every app shows raw field names.

## ⚠️ Read them as two commits, and check whether either is already ruled

Defect 1 is a **declared-versus-enforced disagreement with THREE faces** — the spec's docs, the renderer's docs, and the runtime — and they do not merely differ in strictness, they differ in *direction*: the docs promise tolerance and the code throws. That is not a bug you fix by picking the code's side or the docs' side without evidence. **Find out which was intended** before repairing: `git log -S` on the throw, and read what the spec actually declares `group` to mean.

⛔ Do not assume "the docs are wrong" because the code is the thing that runs. This repo has filed the opposite verdict repeatedly this week — objectui#7735, objectui#7361, objectui#8505 are all cases where the *declaration* was right and the runtime had quietly stopped honouring it.

Defect 2 has a different shape: a fallback chain that bottoms out in a raw field name. ⚠️ Check whether a **non-i18n** label source already exists on the field definition (`label`, `title`, or the object schema's own) before adding one — objectui#8413 measured a case where the help text described a slicing behaviour no code performed, i.e. the platform's own metadata was already carrying the answer.

## ⭐ The blast radius is what makes this p1

*"Takes every sibling section down"* means one authored key blanks an entire record page. Whatever you do, pin that specifically: **a bad `group` on one section must not remove the sections that are fine.** That is the assertion a reviewer will look for and it is the one that must survive your caricature.

The caricature here is a repair that catches the throw and renders nothing — the page stops crashing and silently loses the section. It passes any *"the page no longer throws"* assertion. **Your non-regression axis is that the well-formed sections still render their fields, with their labels**, and that is what carries the weight.

**Run the caricature, do not predict it.** Twelve measurements in this repo this week found the assertion one expects to discriminate is not the one that does. ⚠️ And confirm each discriminating assertion actually **runs** in the leg it was written for — objectui#8506, objectui#8514, objectui#8517 and objectui#8530 each found an assertion that never executed because something earlier reddened first, or because a `@ts-expect-error` was absorbing a different error. **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.**

⚠️ **Do not find your assertion target by the thing you are changing.** If the caricature can erase what your harness navigates by, the harness dies first and the pin measures nothing while reading as a strong refusal (objectui#8504; objectui#8526 hit the positional variant — a caricature's inserted sibling shifted `children[1]`). Prove it with a harness-kill leg whose failure mode is textually distinct.

## Hazards

- Run from the **repo root** with paths, nothing after a bare `--`. `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE` is refused by the guard (objectui#3378); `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently runs `apps/console`'s files. Never `--no-inline-config`.
- ⚠️ `queryByText` throws on **multiple** matches too — use `queryAllByText(...).length`, or scope to one section first. It surfaces as a `waitFor` timeout pointing at the component instead of the query.
- ⚠️ `type-check` only after building the closure, both programs.
- ⚠️ A non-zero exit can mean a **wrong script name**: `pnpm run check:changeset-fixed` → `ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT`; run `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs`.
- ⚠️ `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label**. Write a real changeset.
- ⚠️ `check:control-bytes` does not cover zero-width spaces inside string literals, **and `grep -naP '[\x{200b}…]'` fails outright on this container's grep** in a way that renders as a clean pass — use a Python scanner with a lit control.
- ⚠️ Every grep that can return zero needs a lit control that fires; `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches nothing, use `'packages/*/src/*'`.
- ⚠️ Cite **commit shas, not PR numbers**, when referring to history — I got two PR attributions wrong today by trusting my own account of the session over `git log -S`.
- ⚠️ `packages/plugin-detail` had `DetailSection.tsx` and `HeaderHighlight.tsx` edited today (objectui#8506). Read the merged file.
- Restore **by state** after every ablation with a trap on `EXIT INT TERM` and absolute paths; prove each mutation on disk in both directions.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8584 is out of draft and armed.

### ⭐ You found an on-hold card I should have found before dispatching

**objectui#7051** — open, unassigned, `pm:on-hold`, no linked PR — is *"page `record:details` sections and view `form.sections` resolve `group:` keys via `deriveFieldGroupLayout`"*, i.e. this exact work plus a second surface. Verified: its sequencing gate reads *"objectstack#13855's spec PR is merged **AND objectui has adopted the `@objectstack/*` version carrying it**"*, last touched **2026-09-03**, and your measurement shows spec **17.3.0** is installed and declares `group` on `RecordDetailsProps.sections`.

**The gate has been satisfied and nobody re-measured it.** I dispatched overlapping work without seeing it. That is a PM failure of exactly the kind I named an hour ago — I had stopped reading the backlog — and this is its second instance today, in a different register: not an unread p1, but an unread *hold*.

I am re-scoping #7051 to its remaining half and moving it back to the queue on your measurement.

### ⚠️ The card's three-face framing was a two-face one

I wrote that the spec's docs, the renderer's docs and the runtime disagree. You read the quoted `field-group-layout.ts` sentence **in place** and found it is a **counterfactual** — the rationale for declaring `FIELD_GROUP_KEY_PATTERN` once, i.e. the harm that single-sourcing the key grammar *prevents*. It says nothing about what an authored `group` does.

So the spec declares a working capability; **only objectui's own props description promised a no-op.** The repair direction is unchanged — the declaration was right — but the evidence base is one document, not two, and I would have had you defending a disagreement that does not exist.

Establishing intent by `git log -S` rather than assuming is what made that visible: the crashing expression traces to `e997708419c1` (2026-05-01), **months before** objectstack#13855 declared the key, so the throw was never a deliberate refusal. That is the check I asked for, done properly.

### ⚠️ My non-regression axis does not discriminate — measured, again

I wrote: *"Your non-regression axis is that the well-formed sections still render their fields, with their labels, and that is what carries the weight."*

It **passes under the caricature**, because the siblings are precisely what a caricature preserves. The assertion that separates the right fix from the plausible wrong one is that **the group-referenced section renders its own members**.

I warned about this shape in the same brief, citing objectui#8555, and then wrote an axis with the same defect two paragraphs later. The pattern is now legible: I keep deriving the axis from **the shape of the bug** (what breaks) instead of from **what a plausible wrong fix would still satisfy**. Those are different questions and only the second one produces a discriminating assertion.

### ⭐ Running the caricature changed this PR twice

> With `group` implemented, a group section is resolved into one carrying `fields` **before** `DetailView` sees it — so every group leg passed with the tolerant reader reverted. **The guard for the actual reported crash was dead code by test.**

Two of your own guards were unpinned until the ablation said so, and you added `SECTION_WITHOUT_MEMBERS_IS_BOUNDED` specifically to pin the one that had no coverage. *"Predicting it would have shipped an untested guard"* is the sentence I want in front of the next dev who thinks a caricature is a formality.

### ⭐ Two containment findings the card could not have known

- **An error boundary alone cannot meet acceptance 2.** The reported crash throws inside a `useMemo` in `DetailView`'s **own body**, above the section loop and outside every per-section subtree, so React's boundary cannot reach it. Two layers, each pinned by a different leg.
- **A fixture that looks like it tests the boundary may not reach it.** Your first one threw from a `name` getter — read by `normaliseField` / `columnIdentity` **inside the renderer**, above every boundary — and failed with the raw error. Throwing from `value`, whose first read is `DetailSection`'s own, is the boundary's real subtree. That belongs on the standing list next to "do not navigate by the thing you are changing": *do not throw from a property that is read above the boundary you are testing.*

Also noted: my hazard about `DetailSection.tsx` / `HeaderHighlight.tsx` **did not bite** — both defects live in `renderers/record-details.tsx` and `DetailView.tsx`. Saying so rather than letting an unfired warning look prescient is the right reporting.

### objectui#8583

Filed correctly, and one detail in it is worth more than the card: **vitest was green on the offending literal because it strips types; only `type-check` saw it.** That is the exact inverse of objectui#8571, where `type-check` could not see the defect and only a source-plus-DOM pin could. Two cards, one day, opposite directions — the lesson is that *which* instrument discriminates is itself a measurement, never a default. Both are now on the standing list.

Moving only the two members you needed (`fields` to optional, `group` added) and leaving the other six plus `collapsed`'s fate to their own decision is the right seam: narrowing a published type is a ruling, not a tidy.

### Also accepted

- Both defects **reproduced on the pinned base before any edit**, with the verbatim error and the empty `document.body.textContent` — so the "after" has a real "before".
- The discarded ablation reading: `grep -c -F` treating a multi-line pattern as a **list** of patterns reported "18x" for a mutation that had in fact landed. Replaced with exact substring counting and re-run. That is the fourth dead-instrument catch this week and the second involving `grep`'s multi-line behaviour.
- Each discriminating assertion confirmed to **execute** in its leg **by failing line number** — including `RUNG_1_BUNDLE_WINS` reddening at its *third* assertion, which proves the first two ran rather than short-circuiting.
- `check:sdui-registration-pins` recorded **NOT MEASURED** with the script's own *"this is not a pass"* message quoted, rather than counted as green.
